proposed.explanation:
Telecom Egypt's balance sheet is clearly getting stronger from FY2024 to FY2025. Total equity grew by roughly 38.6% (from 45,937,991,000 to 63,687,826,000 EGP), while total liabilities grew only about 6.7% (from 152,014,797,000 to 162,194,701,000 EGP). The debt-to-equity ratio improved from about 3.31 to 2.55, and the equity-to-assets ratio rose from roughly 23.2% to 28.2%. Cash and cash equivalents remained stable at around 8.3 billion EGP. All of these point to a strengthening balance sheet, which aligns with your goal of owning solid companies over a 5-year horizon.

However, I cannot recommend buying additional ETEL shares. Your current ETEL position (200 shares × 141.95 = 28,390 EGP) already represents about 58.7% of your total portfolio value (28,390 + 20,000 cash = 48,390 EGP). The diversification rule caps any single company at 50% of total portfolio value, and ETEL is already above that threshold. Buying even one more share would increase concentration further. To add to ETEL in the future, you would first need to either sell some ETEL to bring it below 50% (which contradicts your wish to add) or add other positions to dilute the weight.

Given that the balance sheet is strengthening, you have a 5-year horizon, and you want to own solid companies, the appropriate action is to hold your existing 200 shares. You are not selling because the fundamentals are improving, and you are not buying because the concentration limit is already breached. Keep your 20,000 EGP cash available for a future diversifying opportunity. Note that this analysis is based solely on the balance-sheet items provided; income-statement performance, dividend history, and sector risks are not covered here and could affect the overall investment case.
